reserveReview.rationale: The retained fallback rows were authored on September 29 from the July 31 Deloitte examination, but the two deposit percentages were extrapolated using an August 6 weekly-disclosure bank mix. The July examination reports aggregate cash and settlement adjustments, not the SIFI/non-SIFI split. The four rows therefore are not an independently examined composition at a single date; their compositionAsOf has been removed rather than renewed. Both bank slices retain their existing asset classification. The August 31 examination and September 24 itemized weekly disclosure were fetched on October 1; a replacement composition requiring percentage arithmetic is proposed for second-round validation, not applied.
reserveReview.compositionBasis: Historical July 31 examined aggregate balances with an extrapolated August 6 bank-deposit split; retained pending validation of a dated replacement
reserveReview.knownUnknownExposure: All examined reserve assets are classified (U.S. Treasuries, overnight Treasury repos, cash at regulated financial institutions). The SIFI vs non-SIFI split of the examined cash is not disclosed by the examination and is carried from the Aug 06, 2026 weekly-disclosure deposit mix; individual bank and repo counterparties are not named.

custodyProfile.uncertainty: Circle's 2025 Form 10-K states approximately 88% of USDC reserves sat in the BlackRock-managed Circle Reserve Fund (SEC-registered 2a-7 government money market fund) whose assets are held in the custody of BNY as of 2025-12-31; the remainder is cash at global banks, primarily systemically important institutions, whose individual names and shares are undisclosed. The 10-K states reserves are held in accounts titled FBO holders of USDC and that Circle does not lend, borrow against, or encumber the reserves, with applicable state regimes prohibiting lending, pledging, rehypothecating, or otherwise encumbering them. The same filing cautions that no court has ruled on stablecoin reserve treatment in an issuer bankruptcy, so bankruptcy remoteness stays contractual-only; custodian-failure replacement terms remain undisclosed.
